bigPicture: The Gulf war flared again overnight: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain and that a gas tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, while President Trump said Gulf allies asked him to hold off new strikes. Oil had already jumped 3.3% to about $96 on Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi oil sites. Wall Street slipped 0.4% as Nvidia closed 4.3% lower after its CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and the US 10-year yield rose to 5.12% on bets the Fed will raise rates. In diplomacy, Zelensky and US envoy Jared Kushner said Europe will join the next round of Russia–Ukraine talks, as Russia reported one of the largest Ukrainian drone attacks of the year.

glossary.def: An elite branch of Iran's armed forces, separate from the regular army, that answers to the Supreme Leader and runs Iran's naval operations in the Gulf.
glossary.example: The IRGC said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain.

glossary.def: An explosive device placed in the water that detonates when a ship touches or passes near it; it threatens every vessel on a route, not just one target.
glossary.example: Iran said an LPG tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz.

glossary.def: The official closing price of a futures contract for the day, used to value traders' positions.
glossary.example: Brent settled at $95.82 a barrel on Thursday.

glossary.def: A first, quick estimate of an economic statistic based on incomplete data, published early and revised later.
glossary.example: GUS's flash estimate put Poland's Q3 growth at 3.5%; the fuller estimate is due on 30 November.

glossary.def: Data corrected for regular patterns that repeat each year (holidays, weather, number of working days), so one period can be compared fairly with the previous one.
glossary.example: Poland's GDP grew 0.8% quarter on quarter, seasonally adjusted.

glossary.def: The 1970 treaty under which states without nuclear weapons promise not to build them and accept IAEA inspections, in return for access to peaceful nuclear technology.
glossary.example: Iran's Assembly of Experts said studying an NPT exit has become necessary.

glossary.def: A small, fast warship, smaller than a frigate; some carry long-range cruise missiles.
glossary.example: Ukraine's SBU said it hit the Russian corvette Naro-Fominsk.

glossary.def: The right of people to form and join groups such as parties, unions and clubs; it can be limited by law, for example when a group is formed to commit crimes.
glossary.example: A Spanish court suspended Núcleo Nacional during a hate-crime investigation.

glossary.def: A scale that turns measured concentrations of pollutants such as fine particles (PM2.5) into a single number and health category; on India's scale, above 400 is 'severe'.
glossary.example: Delhi's average AQI was 403 on Friday morning.

glossary.def: A measure of the prices producers receive for their goods at the 'factory gate', before retail; it often signals cost pressures that may later reach consumers.
glossary.example: China's PPI rose 5.7% in October while consumer prices rose 0.7%.

glossary.def: China's benchmark lending rate, compiled monthly from banks' quotes under the central bank's guidance; the five-year LPR is the reference for most mortgages.
glossary.example: The one-year LPR has been 3.00% and the five-year 3.50% for 17 months.

glossary.def: An accounting identity: a country's saving minus its domestic investment equals its current-account balance (roughly net exports).
glossary.example: China saves more than it invests at home, matched by a trade surplus of $1.04 trillion in Jan–Oct 2026.

glossary.def: A group of 17 metals used in powerful magnets and electronics; not especially rare in the crust, but hard to separate and refine.
glossary.example: The IEA says China does about 91% of rare-earth refining.

glossary.def: The shift societies make from high birth and death rates to low ones as they grow richer, which slows and eventually stops population growth.
glossary.example: It is why the 1960 'Doomsday' population curve stopped matching reality in the 1990s.

quiz.explain: According to IRNA, quoted by AP, the Guard called the radar attack a warning after a US strike on a telecoms tower in the Iranian port of Sirik. The claim could not be independently verified.

To protest Bahrain joining the Ukraine talks
Because a US tanker hit a mine near Bahrain

quiz.explain: A mine threat applies to every ship on the route, so insurance costs rise and some ships stay away, which reduces supply and raises prices.

Mines make oil cheaper by slowing tankers down
Owners and insurers treat the whole route as dangerous, so many ships avoid it or pay much more to insure
Mines block only LPG tankers, not oil tankers

Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi oil sites, Iran's claims of tanker explosions in Hormuz, and Trump saying the US doesn't need a deal with Iran

They carry US oil to Asia

stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain and that a gas tanker hit a mine in Hormuz; Trump says Gulf allies asked him to hold off
stories.what: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said early on Friday that it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, calling it a 'serious warning' after a US strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, a port in southern Iran, AP reported, citing Iran's IRNA news agency. AP said it was Iran's first claim of hitting a facility in Bahrain since September; Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's 5th Fleet. The IRGC also said a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker struck a sea mine and exploded in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings; the UK's maritime monitoring agency UKMTO had no immediate report of it, and neither claim could be independently verified. President Donald Trump said he held off on further strikes on Iran at the request of Gulf allies, hours after saying he would not hesitate to strike again, Al Jazeera reported.
stories.why: The US–Israeli air war with Iran began in late February, and since then Iran has repeatedly targeted tankers in the strait and US bases in Arab Gulf states. A direct hit on US military equipment in a Gulf country raises the risk of a new round of US strikes, while Gulf states that host US forces fear being drawn in, which, according to Trump's own account, is why they urged restraint. Mines are especially disruptive because ship owners and insurers treat a whole route as dangerous, not just one ship.

stories.what: Brent crude, the international benchmark, settled on Thursday at $95.82 a barrel, up $3.06 or 3.3%, and US crude (WTI) at $88.74, up 2.6%, Reuters reported; both were still about 2.5% lower for the week. Prices first fell, then rebounded after President Trump posted that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran. Yemen's Houthi movement claimed drone and missile attacks on Pumping Station No. 7 of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, an oil facility in the Red Sea port of Yanbu and an Aramco building in Riyadh; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones (two according to Reuters, four according to Xinhua; sources differ), and the claims could not be independently verified. Iran's military also said tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings. Early on Friday Brent traded around $96.
stories.why: The East-West pipeline and Yanbu matter because they are Saudi Arabia's way of exporting oil to the Red Sea while avoiding the Strait of Hormuz; threats to both routes at once reduce the world's spare options. Analyst Timothy Snyder of Matador Economics told Reuters that attacks on shipping and Russia–Ukraine strikes on energy sites are starting to add price pressure. Rising US stockpiles and higher OPEC+ output in October, reported by Reuters, are pulling the other way, which is why prices are still down on the week.

stories.title: Iranian boxer on death row, Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, receives the Magnitsky human-rights award in London
stories.what: Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, a boxer and coach from Mashhad arrested after Iran's 2019 protests, was named the 2026 Magnitsky Award winner for Outstanding Human Rights Activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday, Fox News reported. He was sentenced to death for 'corruption on earth' over alleged arson; Iran's Supreme Court upheld the sentence in October 2025, and his lawyer announced a stay of execution in December 2025. Amnesty International says the charge does not meet international standards for clearly defined offences.
stories.why: International awards aim to raise the political cost of an execution for the government carrying it out.
